headline: Ends the national emergency regarding Iraq that began in 1990 and changes three later executive orders about Iraq.
what_it_does: This order ends the national emergency with respect to Iraq that was declared in Executive Order 12722. That 1990 emergency was the legal basis for certain US sanctions on Iraq. The order also changes three later executive orders about Iraq (13290, 13303, and 13315). The title does not explain what those changes are.

who_it_affects.group: US businesses and individuals dealing with Iraq
who_it_affects.how: Rules tied to the 1990 emergency no longer apply, which may change what dealings with Iraq are allowed.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies that enforce sanctions, such as the Treasury Department
who_it_affects.how: They must adjust how they carry out the Iraq-related orders that were ended or changed.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed July 29, 2004; the title does not give a separate effective date.
